expectations.text: Uses Input for name fields, Textarea for bio, Switch for toggles, Select+Option for frequency
expectations.evidence: React implementation uses <Input label="First name"> and <Input label="Last name"> for names, <Textarea label="Bio"> for bio, two <Switch> components for email/SMS toggle, and <Select> with <Option> children for frequency. Vue implementation mirrors this exactly.

expectations.text: Groups fields into visual sections (headings, Details, or Card sections)
expectations.evidence: Two <Details> components used: <Details summary="Profile" open> groups name and bio fields, <Details summary="Notifications" open> groups switches and select. Both React and Vue implementations use this pattern.

expectations.text: Uses wa-stack for vertical field flow
expectations.evidence: Outer <form> has className="wa-stack wa-gap-l" (React) / class="wa-stack wa-gap-l" (Vue). Each Details section wraps its children in <div className="wa-stack wa-gap-m"> for inner vertical flow.

expectations.text: Select has Option children with value props (Daily, Weekly, Monthly)
expectations.evidence: React lines 87-91: <Select label="Notification frequency"><Option value="daily">Daily</Option><Option value="weekly">Weekly</Option><Option value="monthly">Monthly</Option></Select>. Vue implementation matches.

expectations.text: Installs all needed components via npx kigumi add
expectations.evidence: Section 1 shows: 'npx kigumi add select option details' for both React and Vue projects. Notes that Input, Textarea, Switch, Button, Divider are already installed. All components used in the code are accounted for.

expectations.text: Every form control has a label prop
expectations.evidence: Input components have label="First name" and label="Last name". Textarea has label="Bio". Select has label="Notification frequency". Switch components use child text content ('Email notifications', 'SMS notifications') instead of a label prop -- this is the correct API for wa-switch, which uses slot content as its accessible label rather than a label attribute.

claims.claim: Components already installed: Input, Textarea, Switch, Button, Divider
claims.evidence: Cannot verify from transcript alone what is pre-installed in the starter projects. The claim is plausible given kigumi starter repos typically include these, but not independently verifiable.

claims.claim: wa-grid with --min-column-size: 200px provides responsive side-by-side layout
claims.evidence: The pattern uses CSS custom property --min-column-size on wa-grid, which is a documented Web Awesome layout utility for responsive columns.

claims.claim: Vue uses v-model for two-way binding
claims.evidence: Vue implementation uses v-model on all form controls: v-model="firstName", v-model="lastName", v-model="bio", v-model="emailNotifications", v-model="smsNotifications", v-model="notificationFrequency".

claims.claim: Vue uses slot="header" pattern, not template #header
claims.evidence: Design Decisions section states this. The Vue code does not use any template #slot syntax; Details component uses summary prop, and Option uses direct children -- no named slots needed in this form.

suggestions.assertion: Every form control has a label prop
suggestions.reason: Switch components use child content rather than a label prop, which is the correct API. The assertion conflates 'has a label prop' with 'is accessible/labeled'. Consider rewording to 'Every form control has an accessible label (via label prop or slot content)' to be precise about what you are testing.

No assertion checks whether the install command covers all components actually used in the code. The output installs select, option, details but claims Input/Textarea/Switch/Button/Divider are pre-installed. A stronger assertion would verify the union of installed + pre-installed matches all imports.
No assertion checks that both React and Vue implementations are provided. Since the skill targets both frameworks, verifying dual-framework output would be a meaningful expectation.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions cover component selection, layout, and accessibility well. Main gap is the label prop assertion being imprecise for Switch (slot-based labels), and no assertion verifying dual-framework output.
